Email me See CentrOS

I sit with the people who do the work, map the process, and build the agent system that takes it over, one gated step at a time. Ten years of shipping software at Coursera, Faire and D2L, plus the operator side: I help run the 23-unit hospitality operation CentrOS is built around, so I know what a workflow looks like from the customer's chair.

What I do in the role

5

  1. Map the real workflowShadow the team, write the process down as steps with owners, inputs and failure cases, and agree on which steps an agent may take alone.
  2. Keep a human on anything irreversibleRisk tiers and approval gates before any side effect, with domain experts (legal, accounting, ops) confirming the calls that need them.
  3. Integrate with what they already runTyped, scoped, idempotent tool calls into CRMs, inboxes, calendars and internal APIs, with audit logs per call.
  4. Prove it with evals, not demosGolden datasets from the customer's own cases, regression gates in CI, and traces over cost, latency and failure modes.
  5. Expand in gates, not a big-bang launchPOC on one workflow, then widen scope only when the evals and the approval stats say it is safe to.

How an engagement runs

4

  1. 1. DiscoveryProcess map, success metric and the list of steps an agent must never take alone.
  2. 2. Proof of conceptOne workflow end-to-end on the customer's real data, behind an approval inbox.
  3. 3. Gated rolloutEvals and approval rates decide each expansion; rollback is one step.
  4. 4. HandoverRunbooks, the eval suite and dashboards the customer's team can own.
